properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 27 at 4:34PM MDT until July 27 at 6:45PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows are possible, flooding
caused by excessive rainfall over the Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar
is possible.

* WHERE...Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar in Ouray County Colorado,
including Dexter and Cutler Creek drainages and Highway 550.

* WHEN...Until 645 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall is possible over the Gold Mountain
Burn Scar which could lead to flash flooding and/or debris flows,
particularly along highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter
Creek. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and
other loose materials.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 432 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Ouray.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.areaDesc: Gunnison, CO; Hinsdale, CO; Ouray, CO

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 27 at 4:30PM MDT until July 27 at 6:30PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Clear Creek County in central Colorado...
West Central Jefferson County in central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 630 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Hazardous travel conditions with very heavy rain causing low
visibility and water on roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 430 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This may cause small stream flooding. Between 0.5
and 1 inch of rain has fallen in under 30 minutes.

- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are expected over
the area in the next hour as the storms move east over the
Evergreen area. This additional rain could result in minor
flooding.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Evergreen, Brookvale, Floyd Hill, Bergen Park, Blue Valley,
Kittredge and Wah Keeney Park.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 27 at 4:21PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 421 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Creede, or 46 miles south of Gunnison, moving north at 5 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and half inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

This storm will remain over mainly rural areas of southwestern
Saguache and northeastern Mineral Counties.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 27 at 4:04PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 404 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Blue Valley, or 31 miles west of Denver, moving east at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and half inch size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Wind and hail could lead to low visibility and hazardous
driving conditions along I-70 and other travel routes in
eastern Clear Creek, northwest Jefferson, and southeast
Gilpin Counties.

Locations impacted include...
Evergreen, Idaho Springs, Blue Valley, Floyd Hill, Brookvale,
Bergen Park, Kittredge, Echo Lake and Wah Keeney Park.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 27 at 3:30PM MDT until July 27 at 6:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Garfield County in west central Colorado...

* Until 630 PM MDT.

* At 330 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain above Roan Creek. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has
fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 3 inches in 1 hour.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Thunderstorms producing flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of creeks and streams, county roads.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
mainly rural areas of South Central Garfield County along Roan
Creek
